text: The bioarchaeological research on the 20 skeletons that have been found in the graveyard surrounding the Hrísbrú church shows that the inhabitants from the time of colonization lived a hard life, suffering from such diseases as tuberculosis and cancer. As noted by Magnus Guðmundsson, in an interview with Morgunblaðið (The Morning Paper), Egil Skallagrimsson was also suffering from several ailments in the last years of his life. But he had it considerably good with his niece Thordis and her husband Grimr Svertingsson.
